description: Timeless by Tran, a demo he made alone in 32-bit protected-mode assembly, running from its original files in your browser.
about: Timeless is a demo for MS-DOS by Tran (Thomas Pytel), from February 1994. He made all of it, its design, code, graphics and music, in 32-bit protected-mode assembly under PMODE 2.4, the DOS extender he wrote; only the low-level Sound Blaster driver is another's, Dave's (White Shadow).
Here it plays once through, then shows its end picture, of two nude female figures in grayscale, and returns to DOS, after about three and a half minutes in all. Escape ends it at any time.
released: TIMELESS.DOC calls it “a demo in Feb 1994”; its program is dated 26 February 1994.
credits: Design, code, graphics and music by Tran; the low-level Sound Blaster driver by Dave (White Shadow).
terms: “You may distribute and use this demo in any manner you wish, as long as all the original files, unmodified, are included with it.” (TIMELESS.DOC)
accuracy: DosKit starts it with two of its own switches: /S343, for the Gravis UltraSound at port 240 and IRQ 5, which skips its sound card menu, and /L1, which plays it once and then shows its end screen. Without /L it loops until Escape.
Its end screen fades and holds at half speed in some runs, so it returns to DOS after about 201 or about 214 seconds.
Not yet compared with a capture made on real hardware.
imageAlt: Fish and flowers over Timeless's red, mirrored blobs, running in DosKit
